article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Indica / 30% Sativa
Genetics: Hash Plant × Shiva Skunk × SFV OG
Breeder: Sensi Seeds
THC Content: 20.6% r
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: pinene , limonene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Sweet Citrus, Earthy Kush, Fresh Pine
Flowering Time (Indoor): 55–60 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: early October
Indoor Yield: 425–475 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 550+ g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to Moderate

Coffee, caramel, fresh pine, and old-fashioned hashish rarely appear together in the same cannabis fragrance, yet Tezla OG brings these contrasting elements into an unusually cohesive aromatic profile. Developed by Sensi Seeds through its Research collection, this indica-dominant hybrid combines three influential genetic families: Hash Plant, Shiva Skunk, and San Fernando Valley OG. The resulting marijuana variety bridges decades of breeding history, connecting traditional Afghan resin production with classic Dutch Skunk genetics and the unmistakable character of California OG.

Compact plants produce numerous dense, conical flowers coated in crystalline trichomes, while the experience moves from lively cerebral euphoria into sustained physical relaxation. Its manageable dimensions, productive lateral branches, and substantial harvest potential make it particularly appealing to cultivators seeking a reliable photoperiod hybrid. Beneath its familiar OG designation lies a distinctive combination of old-school cannabis heritage, sophisticated aromas, and practical growing characteristics.
Genetics and Lineage

Tezla OG originates from a three-way genetic combination involving Hash Plant, Shiva Skunk, and SFV OG, producing a hybrid containing approximately 70% indica and 30% sativa ancestry. Sensi Seeds developed the cultivar to incorporate complementary characteristics from established European and American breeding traditions. Hash Plant provides a foundation of compact growth and abundant resin, Shiva Skunk introduces vigor and substantial branching, and SFV OG contributes the distinctive flowering structure and aromatic complexity associated with California Kush varieties . The breeder identifies all three contributing lines, although the precise sequence of the crosses has not been publicly detailed.

Hash Plant represents one of the most historically significant components of this lineage. The Sensi Seeds version descends from traditional Afghan cannabis selections refined through breeding with Northern Lights #1. These genetics emphasize resin-rich flowers, short internodal spacing, and a deeply earthy fragrance reminiscent of traditional hashish. Shiva Skunk introduces another important chapter of cannabis history through its Northern Lights #5 and Skunk #1 parentage. Originally released during the late 1980s, Shiva Skunk became influential for its robust development, heavy flowering, and combination of musky pungency with sweeter aromatic notes. Skunk #1 itself traces its ancestry to Afghan, Colombian, and Mexican cannabis populations, providing additional genetic diversity.

San Fernando Valley OG completes the composition through the celebrated OG Kush family . Associated with California’s San Fernando Valley, SFV OG is valued for its earthy pine fragrance, pronounced citrus character, and resinous flowering structure. Its influence is especially noticeable in the finished hybrid’s numerous compact, conical buds and lingering Kush flavors. Bringing these three genetic traditions together produces a marijuana plant that retains the physical substance of traditional indica breeding while introducing a brighter sensory character and an initially stimulating experience.
Effects and Experience

The opening stage of the Tezla OG experience offers an interesting contrast to its predominantly indica genetics. Rather than immediately producing physical heaviness, the initial effects may involve a noticeable increase in mental brightness and an enjoyable sense of euphoria. Conversation can become more engaging, music may seem unusually absorbing, and familiar recreational activities can take on a more entertaining quality. This early cerebral stimulation generally feels smoother than the pronounced intensity associated with certain Haze varieties. A comfortable improvement in mood accompanies the mental uplift, creating an atmosphere suited to casual social interaction or relaxed creative activities.

Physical relaxation gradually becomes the dominant sensation as intoxication progresses. Muscles may feel less tense, while the body develops an increasingly comfortable heaviness. The initial mental stimulation slowly gives way to a quieter state of contentment, allowing the experience to transition naturally into restful activities. At moderate doses, consumers may remain conversational and attentive despite noticeable bodily relaxation. Larger amounts can encourage prolonged stillness and drowsiness, particularly among individuals with limited THC tolerance. A documented breeder cultivation produced flowers containing 20.6% THC, confirming substantial psychoactive potential. Excessive exposure may produce dizziness, anxiety, dry mouth, impaired coordination, or temporary difficulty concentrating. The strength and progression of the effects depend on cannabinoid composition, dosage, and individual sensitivity.
Medical Benefits

The relaxing properties of Tezla OG may interest medical marijuana patients seeking temporary relief from certain forms of physical discomfort. Some THC-containing cannabis products have demonstrated modest benefits for particular chronic pain conditions, especially neuropathic pain. The cultivar’s progression toward sustained bodily calm may appeal to individuals who experience discomfort during periods of rest or after physically demanding activities. Its initially uplifting character may also provide a subjective sense of emotional comfort before the heavier effects develop. However, controlled clinical research evaluating this particular strain has not been published, and its genetic background cannot establish effectiveness for pain, muscle spasms, or inflammatory conditions.

Stress-related symptoms and difficulty unwinding represent additional areas of potential interest. The opening euphoria may temporarily improve subjective mood, while progressive physical relaxation could make quiet evening activities more comfortable. Some consumers may find the later effects compatible with bedtime routines, although sedation does not necessarily indicate improved sleep quality. Research concerning long-term cannabis use for insomnia remains mixed, and regular THC exposure can produce tolerance or dependence. High-potency marijuana may also worsen anxiety, panic, or other psychiatric symptoms in susceptible individuals.

Medical suitability depends on laboratory-tested cannabinoid concentrations, personal health history, and possible medication interactions. THC can impair judgment, influence cardiovascular responses, and intensify the effects of certain sedating medications. Patients considering cannabis for symptom management should consult a qualified healthcare professional rather than relying exclusively on recreational strain descriptions. Although this cultivar may provide subjective relief for some individuals, it should not replace established medical treatments.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The fragrance of Tezla OG develops through several noticeably different aromatic layers. During vegetative growth, the plant produces relatively restrained floral and herbal impressions accompanied by subtle fruit sweetness. As flowering progresses, its aroma becomes deeper and more pungent, introducing damp earth, fresh-cut pine, and traditional Kush characteristics. Mature flowers release a distinctive combination of sweet berries and resinous wood, while the darker components resemble sandalwood, roasted coffee, and warm spice. A creamy caramel impression adds unexpected softness to the fragrance, creating a contrast between confectionery sweetness and the heavier aromatic qualities inherited from its Afghan and OG ancestry.

After drying and curing , the sensory profile becomes more concentrated. Breaking apart the dense flowers releases pronounced earthy pine and sweet fruit, followed by woody fragrance and subtle roasted notes. During consumption, the opening flavor tends to emphasize zesty citrus, creating a brighter impression than the aroma might suggest. This initial sweetness gradually gives way to earthy Kush, aromatic pine, and mild herbal spice. The lingering finish carries a recognizable resinous character associated with traditional OG genetics. Proper post-harvest handling is important because excessive heat, prolonged oxygen exposure, and inadequate storage can diminish the more delicate citrus and fruit qualities.

A comprehensive laboratory-confirmed terpene profile has not been established for the cultivar. Pinene could contribute to the pronounced pine fragrance, while limonene may influence the citrus impressions. Myrcene and beta-caryophyllene are plausible contributors to its earthy, herbal, and spicy qualities, although their presence and relative concentrations require analytical confirmation. The coffee, caramel, and sandalwood characteristics may involve additional volatile compounds that cannot be identified reliably through aroma alone. The strain’s distinctive fragrance therefore reflects a complex interaction of aromatic substances rather than one confirmed dominant terpene.
Growing Information

Tezla OG develops into a compact cannabis plant with vigorous lateral branching and closely spaced internodes. The young plant initially displays a distinctly indica-oriented structure, producing broad foliage and dense vegetative growth around a strong central stem. As flowering approaches, the lateral branches extend more noticeably, creating a wider canopy than the relatively short stature might suggest. Indoor specimens typically reach approximately 80–120 centimeters, while outdoor plants can exceed 100 centimeters under favorable conditions. Mature flowers form numerous small, tightly packed, conical clusters resembling the structure associated with SFV OG. Dark green foliage may develop purple highlights during the final weeks of flowering, contrasting with orange pistils and a generous coating of crystalline trichomes.

The breeder estimates an indoor flowering period of approximately 55–60 days, although individual plants may require additional time. In a documented Sensi Seeds cultivation, flowering continued for 73 days, with the complete growth cycle lasting 94 days. That specimen reached 102 centimeters and produced approximately 94 grams of dried flower containing 20.6% THC. Under favorable indoor conditions, projected yields range from 425–475 grams per square meter. Outdoor plants may produce more than 550 grams each in suitable environments. These figures represent cultivation potential rather than guaranteed production, since lighting, environmental stability, plant development , and growing space influence final harvest weight.

A warm, sunny environment resembling a Mediterranean climate provides favorable outdoor conditions, particularly where summer temperatures remain consistent and autumn rainfall is limited. Indoors, the relatively compact height makes the cultivar suitable for spaces with restricted vertical clearance. Its lateral branching responds well to Screen of Green arrangements, while Sea of Green cultivation can take advantage of the numerous flowering sites. Supercropping and selective removal of lower growth are additional options for experienced growers. Heavy buds may require branch support as flowering progresses, since slender lateral stems can bend beneath developing flowers. Dense foliage also makes adequate airflow important, especially near harvest when moisture accumulation may encourage fungal problems. These manageable characteristics make the plant accessible to beginners while offering experienced cultivators opportunities for more deliberate canopy management.
FAQ
Is Tezla OG an indica or sativa strain?

Tezla OG is an indica-dominant hybrid containing approximately 70% indica and 30% sativa genetics. Its ancestry combines Hash Plant, Shiva Skunk, and SFV OG. Although the plant expresses compact indica-oriented growth, the experience generally begins with cerebral euphoria before transitioning into sustained physical relaxation. The sativa influence is also apparent in its vigorous lateral branching.
What is the THC percentage of Tezla OG?

A documented Sensi Seeds cultivation produced dried flowers containing 20.6% THC. This places the cultivar within the high-potency category, although individual harvests may produce different cannabinoid concentrations. Laboratory testing of the specific cannabis product provides the most dependable indication of strength.
What does Tezla OG taste like?

The flavor combines sweet citrus, earthy Kush, fresh pine, and subtle herbal spice. Its aroma is considerably more elaborate, introducing sweet berries, sandalwood, caramel, and roasted coffee impressions. The citrus character dominates the opening taste, while traditional earthy OG qualities become more noticeable toward the finish.
Does Tezla OG make you sleepy?

The cultivar can produce drowsiness, particularly during the later stages of intoxication or after larger doses. Its effects generally begin with an uplifting mental sensation before developing into substantial bodily relaxation. Moderate consumption may remain comfortable without immediately causing pronounced sedation, although individual responses depend on THC tolerance and dosage.
How long does Tezla OG take to flower?

The breeder lists approximately 55–60 days of indoor flowering, although a documented cultivation required 73 days. Plants commonly reach 80–120 centimeters indoors and may produce 425–475 grams per square meter under favorable conditions. Outdoor yields can exceed 550 grams per plant, depending on the growing environment and seasonal conditions.
Final Thoughts on Tezla OG

Tezla OG brings together three influential branches of cannabis breeding without losing the recognizable characteristics of its individual ancestors. Hash Plant contributes the resinous structure and earthy depth of Afghan genetics, Shiva Skunk supplies vigorous growth and productive branching, and SFV OG introduces the distinctive citrus-pine character associated with California Kush. The resulting flowers offer an unusually elaborate aromatic combination of sandalwood, sweet berries, caramel, coffee, and traditional marijuana pungency.

For consumers, the primary attraction lies in the gradual transition from enjoyable cerebral euphoria into long-lasting physical comfort. Growers benefit from manageable plant dimensions, numerous productive flowering sites, and substantial yield potential without unusually complicated cultivation requirements. With documented THC potency exceeding 20%, visually attractive flowers, and a rich genetic history, Tezla OG demonstrates the continuing relevance of established cannabis breeding lines. Its combination of dependable growth, sophisticated aromas, and balanced psychoactive progression gives this indica-dominant hybrid a distinctive identity within the broader OG Kush family.
